q-143471.name: Question 1
q-143471.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(5,\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample 

$$
{x}_{1}=5,\,{x}_{2}=3,\,{x}_{3}=2,\,{x}_{4}=1.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡a+b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +c\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
q-143471.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=5$ as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{N}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{N-x},\,x=0,1,…,N \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{5-x},\,x=0,1,…,5.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{5-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{5-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(5-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(5-{x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(5n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

Now, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{1}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{2}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{3}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{4}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, our expression for $l(\theta )$ becomes

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}))+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(5n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{{x}_{i}}) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{5})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{3})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{2})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{5}{1}) \\  & =1\cdot 10\cdot 10\cdot 5 \\  & =500,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
S=5+3+2+1=11.
$$

Substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta )$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(500)+11\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(5\cdot 4-11)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(500)+11\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +9\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=500+11+9=520.
$$

Suppose X1,X2,X3,X4 is an I.I.D random sample with Xi∼B(5,θ) with unknown probability of success θ. You're given the particular sample x1=5,x2=3,x3=2,x4=1. The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by l(θ)=ln⁡a+bln⁡θ+cln⁡(1−θ).

Find the value of a+b+c.

a
510
b
450
c
500
d
520
e
480
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if X1,X2,…,Xn are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function f(x;θ), where θ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample x1,x2,…,xn is l(θ)=ln⁡L(θ)=ln⁡(∏i=1nf(xi,θ))=∑i=1nln⁡(f(xi,θ)).

In our case, we are given a sample of n=4 independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success θ and N=5 as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is f(x,θ)=(Nx)θx(1−θ)N−x,x=0,1,…,N=(5x)θx(1−θ)5−x,x=0,1,…,5.

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows: l(θ)=∑i=1nln⁡((5xi)θxi(1−θ)5−xi)=∑i=1nln⁡(5xi)+ln⁡(θxi)+ln⁡((1−θ)5−xi)=∑i=1nln⁡(5xi)+∑i=1nxiln⁡θ+∑i=1n(5−xi)ln⁡(1−θ)=∑i=1nln⁡(5xi)+ln⁡θ∑i=1nxi+ln⁡(1−θ)∑i=1n(5−xi)=∑i=1nln⁡(5xi)+Sln⁡θ+(5n−S)ln⁡(1−θ) where S=∑i=1nxi.

Now, note that

∑i=1nln⁡(5xi)=ln⁡(5x1)+ln⁡(5x2)+ln⁡(5x3)+ln⁡(5x4)=ln⁡(∏i=1n(5xi)).

So, our expression for l(θ) becomes

l(θ)=ln⁡(∏i=1n(5xi))+Sln⁡θ+(5n−S)ln⁡(1−θ).

Now, using the sample data with n=4, we have ∏i=1n(5xi)=(55)⋅(53)⋅(52)⋅(51)=1⋅10⋅10⋅5=500,

and S=5+3+2+1=11.

Substituting the above values into our expression for l(θ), we get

l(θ)=ln⁡(500)+11ln⁡θ+(5⋅4−11)ln⁡(1−θ)=ln⁡(500)+11ln⁡θ+9ln⁡(1−θ).

Finally,

a+b+c=500+11+9=520.

q-143473.name: Question 2
q-143473.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼Po(\theta )$ with unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample

$$
{x}_{1}=3,\,{x}_{2}=4,\,{x}_{3}=2.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=a\theta +b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡c.
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
q-143473.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent Poisson random variables with unknown parameter $\theta .$ Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & ={e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{x}}{x!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{{x}_{i}}}{{x}_{i}!}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta })+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-n\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}!)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}! & =3!\cdot 4!\cdot 2!=6\cdot 24\cdot 2=288, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =3+4+2=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta ),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-3\theta +9\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡288.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=-3+9+288=294.
$$

q-159843.name: Question 3
q-159843.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼Po(\theta )$ with unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample

$$
{x}_{1}=4,\,{x}_{2}=1,\,{x}_{3}=0,\,{x}_{4}=2.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=a\theta +b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡c.
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$

*Hint: The probability mass function for a Poisson distribution is given by* 

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\theta }^{x}{e}^{-\theta }}{x!},\,x=0,1,2,…
$$
q-159843.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent Poisson random variables with unknown parameter $\theta .$ Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & ={e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{x}}{x!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{{x}_{i}}}{{x}_{i}!}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta })+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-n\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}!)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}! & =4!\cdot 1!\cdot 0!\cdot 2!=24\cdot 1\cdot 1\cdot 2=48, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =4+1+0+2=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta ),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-4\theta +7\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡48.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=-4+7+48=51.
$$

q-159844.name: Question 4
q-159844.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼Po(\theta )$ with unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample

$$
{x}_{1}=1,\,{x}_{2}=6,\,{x}_{3}=1.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=a\theta +b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡c.
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
q-159844.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent Poisson random variables with unknown parameter $\theta .$ Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & ={e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{x}}{x!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta }\cdot \frac{{\theta }^{{x}_{i}}}{{x}_{i}!}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta })+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\theta )+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}1+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}_{i}!) \\  & =-n\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}-\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}!)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}! & =1!\cdot 6!\cdot 1!=1\cdot 720\cdot 1=720, \\ {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =1+6+1=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta ),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-3\theta +8\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡720.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=-3+8+720=725.
$$

q-159904.name: Question 5
q-159904.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(4,\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample 

$$
{x}_{1}=1,\,{x}_{2}=2,\,{x}_{3}=3,\,{x}_{4}=4.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡a+b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +c\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$
q-159904.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=4$ as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{N}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{N-x},\,x=0,1,…,N \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{4-x},\,x=0,1,…,4.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{4-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{4-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}})+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(4-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(4-{x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}})+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(4n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

Now, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{1}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{2}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{3}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{4}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, our expression for $l(\theta )$ becomes

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}}))+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(4n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{{x}_{i}}) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{1})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{2})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{3})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{4}{4}) \\  & =4\cdot 6\cdot 4\cdot 1 \\  & =96,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
S=1+2+3+4=10.
$$

Substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta )$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(96)+10\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(4\cdot 4-10)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(96)+10\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +6\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=96+10+6=112.
$$

So, our expression for l(θ) becomes l(θ)=ln⁡(∏i=1n(4xi))+Sln⁡θ+(4n−S)ln⁡(1−θ).

Now, using the sample data with n=4, we have ∏i=1n(4xi)=(41)⋅(42)⋅(43)⋅(44)=4⋅6⋅4⋅1=96,

and S=1+2+3+4=10.
